reviews.review:
If you like Risk of Rain 2, you'll probably like this game!

The devs seem active and they're taking players' feedback into consideration, which is a huge plus. So far, they've had frequent updates and their passion for the project shows. THE GAME RUNS SMOOTHLY! No game breaking or frustrating bugs, which is a good sign. The controls are pretty intuitive. The level progression feels natural.

It's in EA, so they're still adding content at the time of this review. I feel like there should be more playable characters from the start since it's up to 8 players (thank you!) but, with what the amount they have now, it seems like a decent roster, especially when you factor in balancing and making each character unique. They're already working on more characters, which is awesome.

The levels are nice. You have 3 "days" to get your run for a level complete, and the day/night cycle adds variety in the enemies, which I like. There were a few times where I worried I might take fall damage from an enemy attack and was pleasantly surprised when that didn't happen. I really like the chest and reward varieties so far too.

There's already a decent variety of enemies and I like that some features can produce more (and more) of them and they're clearly marked. Nothing feels cheap or unwarranted in the game, which is nice! I can't say I'm currently a fan of the tornado AOEs some enemies can produce because they feel too large/they obscure too much of the screen but, it's a mild complaint.

Overall, a very well made EA title. 
It looks like the game is estimated to be in EA for a year or less, which shows they have a plan in mind and they're executing it (as it should be).

Thanks for the awesome time so far, devs!
reviews.developer_response: Thanks for the thoughtful and thorough review. We're glad you're a member of the community!

reviews.review:
Finally beat it on Normal difficulty. This game is great so far and full of potential, very excited to see what it has to offer in the future. It doesn't let loose as much as Risk of Rain, but instead reminds me more of Ravenswatch in terms of the day night cycle and level/questing struture.

As of writing, there's certainly some balancing problems with class tuning. It's clear the mage is the strongest class as their abilities just lend best to this style of game, while melee characters struggle most. There's definitely some room to explore more varied base stats tuning for these diferent playstyles, especially as you go further in. Some bosses just seem downright impossible to me without range options that the class you chose may not be built for.

Progression is tough and punishing, which is what the game is going for. Should be expected in a roguelike and it's excellent here. After a few runs, the earlier enemies become less and less problematic. However, I feel that I also opened fewer and fewer chests over time because the economy scaling didn't quite match my progression. In multiplayer anyways, things got more expensive faster than we were able to earn. It may be designed that way for balancing purposes but the appeal of these games to me is getting random items and buffing up. I wish LORT would let loose a little more.

Overall it's a fun time with friends. I played with 5-6 others, which is rare for this type of game to offer, and had a blast. Clearing a run is as exilerating as I imagined, weapons diversity is good at this stage, class distinction makes sense, and progession is intuitive. Bosses are pretty tanky but the earlier ones are cleared quickly with enough permanent progression, while the latter have enough chaos going on that always made me engaged. This game is 100% built for a multiplayer experience and I was totally rewarded for it.

Final comments, I wish there was more ways to interact with my friends. A healer or support class would be neat. Perhaps ways to drop powerups cause as it stands, the benefits seem universal regardless of class when I wish I could see more build variety and ways to sell unwanted powerups/weapons. Devs advertise god runs but I don't really feel I ever experienced anything like that akin to risk of rain as many people compare to so I wouldn't go in expecting it. Chaos, however, is plenty and abundant; very unga bunga.

gud gme. thx devs <3
reviews.developer_response: Thanks for the very detailed review. We'll keep releasing updates to make LORT better for you!

reviews.review:
The core gameplay and design of this game are good and a lot of fun. However, normal mode feels only balanced for 8 players, anything less than that and it doesn't feel like the developers designed it to be beatable without great rng and luck. 

The easy mode is too easy compared to normal mode. The difficulty spike doesn't make sense. So it needs some balancing reworks.
reviews.developer_response: Thanks for the review and heard on the feedback. We will keep improving the difficulty modes. The game is indeed meant to be beaten solo or with less than 8 players. Best thing I can recommend for now is maximize your attribute gain per map, and you will get pretty chadded.
